data.body_html:
The Sotogrande Polo Final 2041 is the crown jewel of the Costa del Sol summer calendar — and arriving by boat from Marbella turns the day into an unforgettable experience. With a Marbella boat rental, you skip the traffic, enjoy a scenic cruise past the Golden Mile and Cabopino, and anchor right next to the polo fields. This guide covers everything you need to know: which boats suit your group, how to book, what's included, and insider tips for the big day.

Why Choose a Marbella Boat Rental for the Polo Final?

Driving to Sotogrande on polo final day means sitting in traffic for an hour or more, then hunting for a parking spot. A private charter from Puerto Banús lets you arrive in style, with a licensed skipper handling navigation while you enjoy drinks and snacks on deck. The sea breeze keeps you cool, and you can anchor with a front-row view of the match. After the final, you cruise back under the sunset — no queues, no stress.

Timing Your Departure for the Polo Final

The Sotogrande Polo Final 2041 typically starts at 16:00. We recommend departing Puerto Banús at 13:00 at the latest. The 25 NM journey takes about 60-75 minutes at cruising speed, leaving you plenty of time to anchor, set up, and enjoy pre-match drinks. After the final (around 18:00-19:00), you can cruise back to Marbella for dinner or continue the party on board.

What to Bring and Wear

Dress smart-casual: linen trousers or chinos with a polo shirt for men, sundresses or elegant separates for women. Deck shoes or espadrilles are best — avoid black soles that can mark the deck. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket for the evening breeze. You're welcome to bring your own food and drinks, though we already provide a selection of beverages and snacks. Glass bottles are allowed, but use plastic cups on deck for safety.

How to Book

Booking is straightforward. For Tier A and B boats, you can reserve directly on our website with the listed prices. For other vessels, contact us via WhatsApp for a custom quote.
